sentences.text: It buys you two days.
Then, on the twelfth night, somebody knocks on the fire exit.
Three knocks, a pause, three more.
The dead do not knock.
There are four of them.
A pickup truck, a tow chain, and a very simple plan.
They saw the lights on day nine.
They know someone is inside.
And they know what is in here with you.
Problem four: the living.
You cannot fight four people.
But you understand something they do not.
If they tear that shutter off, 250 dead walk in right behind them.
And then nobody has a supermarket.
So you do not open the door.
You open the store.
One rope and one bucket, lowered off the back of the roof at 1:30 in the morning.
The first fifteen tins are free.
After that, you trade.
Batteries, fuel, medicine, news.
You worked retail for five years.
You know how to handle difficult customers.
House rule, amended: nobody comes in, but the roof is open.
By day sixteen, there is a queue.
A woman with a baby, two old men with a wheelbarrow, and a girl on a bike who only ever asks for cat food.
On the seventeenth night at nine o'clock, something scratches at the staff entrance.
Metal on metal.
Someone is trying to fit a key in the lock.
It is Rhea.
She is starting her shift, but the lock is full of your broken key.
She works at it for an hour.
The next night, she is back.
She is never late.
On day twenty, the bucket comes up with a note in it.
Pencil, in a child's handwriting.
The men with the truck are done trading.
They are coming tonight.
They want all of it.
Please let us in.
House rule one says nobody comes in.
